question: Your extraction system has a coordinator that sends each section of an insurance claim file to a subagent. When the medical-codes subagent times out on its code lookup, it reports only the failure type "timeout" to the coordinator. The coordinator then re-dispatches the whole section, so the medical-codes subagent re-extracts fields it had already finished and repeats the same failed lookup. Which change to the error report best fixes this?

options.text: Add few-shot examples to the coordinator's system prompt that show it re-dispatching only the failed part of a section after a subagent timeout.
options.reason: The coordinator cannot know which part failed or which fields are done unless the error report includes the attempted query and the partial results.

options.text: Add a numeric error code and a timestamp to the timeout report, so the coordinator can log each failure and track how often the lookup times out.
options.reason: An error code and a timestamp support logging, but they do not tell the coordinator what was attempted, which fields are done or which alternatives exist.

options.text: Replace the failure type with a longer free-text message that describes the timeout in detail and asks the coordinator to handle the section more carefully.
options.reason: A detailed description of the timeout still omits the attempted query, the partial results and the alternatives, which the coordinator needs for an informed recovery decision.

options.text: Add the attempted lookup query, the fields already extracted, and possible alternatives such as a different lookup source, alongside the failure type.
options.reason: Structured error context with what was attempted, partial results and alternatives lets the coordinator skip finished work and choose a different recovery instead of repeating the same lookup.
